text:
maya: Quick sync — small refactor idea for dedicated GPU pool admission. Proposal: two-tier admission (local fast-path at the operator/node level) + global governor for long-term balancing and cost signals. Sketch below.

raj: Quick q — what's the local fast-path exactly?

maya: Local fast-path = operator-side admission using in-memory credits + instantaneous headroom check. No round-trip to central service for common cases. Global governor still owns fairness, global evictions, and cost-driven revocations.

kevin: Sounds promising. How does this interact with prewarm and burst credits today?

maya: Local keeps a small ephemeral burst counter per tenant (60s window). The global reconciler periodically adjusts that counter and can revoke burst credits when cost or utilization signals spike. We keep the on-disk/billing ledger central.

jia: That implies the operator needs a lightweight API surface to answer admit queries, right?

maya: Yes — minimal: /admit?tenant_id=... -> { decision: admit|wait|throttle, reason }. We cache recent admits and keep RTT target < 2ms.

ops-bot: Integration tests for operator-admit API on staging: passed :white_check_mark: (build 2025.11.3)

raj: Example config sketch:
```
admission:
  fast_path:
    enabled: true
    local_granularity: slot
    burst_window_sec: 60
  global_governor:
    sync_interval_sec: 15
    cost_threshold_pct: 120
    eviction_mode: soft
```

maya: Tradeoffs: faster common-case admits, reduced central contention, but more logic in the operator and risk of short-term oversubscribe if reconciliation lags.

kevin: Fairness concern — local fast-path might let high-frequency tenants hog slots and starve lower-priority ones.

maya: Mitigation: token-bucket with priority bands + small jitter on admit windows. Global governor measures longer-term usage and tightens per-tenant ceilings when imbalance observed.

jia: Rollout idea: feature-flag the fast-path as "simulate" first (operators return simulated decisions but don't enforce) for 2 weeks, then opt-in a small set of tenants.

raj: Metrics to track during rollout: local_admit_latency, admit_decision_mismatch_rate, global_reconcile_lag, burst_revocations, p99_inflight_latency, tenant_headroom_violation_count.

maya: I'll draft an RFC + rollout checklist. Need owners for tests, metrics dashboards, and canary tenants.

kevin: I can own the rollout checklist and canary selection.

jia: I'll take the admit API tests and add unit coverage for the token-bucket edge cases.

ops-bot: FYI: related incident retrospective -> https://redwood.atlassian/DEDI-456 (read before rollout)

maya: Thanks all — I'll file the RFC and ping for reviews. Aim to have RFC up by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:

kevin: +1
